history.period: Unverified (local sources call it one of Goa's oldest temples; no sourced construction date found)
history.summary: Temple at Poinguinim village, Canacona taluka, dedicated to Lord Parashurama, the axe-wielding sixth avatar of Vishnu. It is tied to the traditional origin legend of Goa (and of the Konkan/Kerala/Kanara coast): Parashurama reclaimed the land from the sea with an axe-throw. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the 'state' column wrongly holds town names (all five rows are in GOA state); this row's town is the village of Poinguinim, with Canacona as the nearest municipal centre (taluka). Identity confirmed by geocoder and multiple travel sources; the building's age and dynastic origin are unsourced — treat any antique claims as (verify). Deities reportedly face each other within the shrine, an unusual feature noted in a recent Goa documentary.

name: Parshuram Temple
town_description: Poinguinim (also spelled Painginim/Paingyapura) is a village in Canacona taluka, South Goa, about 10 km south-east of Chaudi on NH66 towards Karwar. It is a hinterland temple village in the Western Ghats foothills, also home to the Shri Betal temple known for its triennial Gadyaanchi Jatra.

travel.airport: Dabolim International Airport (GOI), roughly 75 km north-west
travel.railway: Canacona railway station (near Chaudi), about 10 km north-west; Madgaon Junction about 40 km north
travel.road: On NH66 (Panvel-Kanyakumari); village buses stop at Poinguinim; ~10 km south-east of Chaudi

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (cooler, dry season); Parashurama Jayanti (Akshaya Tritiya, April-May) and the annual March jatra for festival atmosphere
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not reliably published — verify locally before visiting
